house_rules: Cache buster ALWAYS: every probe carries a unique query parameter (?cb={{rand}}) so a poisoned entry never collides with real users - collateral poisoning of a shared entry is an incident, not a finding.
Payloads/techniques are canonical forms from the public record, attributed per entry.
Poisoning demonstrations end with an operator-owned fetch confirming the stored entry - never wait for a real user to hit it.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a probe that failed for a listed reason leaves the cache untested, not secure.

entries.probe: GET /?cb={{per-probe-random}} HTTP/1.1 - unique value per request, paired with the probe input under test
entries.oracle: response X-Cache (or Age / timing) flips miss->hit on immediate re-request of the SAME cb value: proves the cache keys the full URL and that you own a private test slot
failure_modes: no X-Cache-style header - use timing or Age differentials with n>=3 before concluding no cache exists
cache normalizes unknown query params OUT of the key - the buster then does NOT isolate you; detect by poisoning a buster and fetching a DIFFERENT one (see CACHE-005)

prerequisites: origin reflects a request header into the response body/headers
that header is NOT part of the cache key
entries.oracle: first fetch stores the marker inside the cached response; second fetch (no header, same cb) replays the marker from cache - the PAIR (inject-then-inherit) is the poison proof
failure_modes: header is keyed (or Vary: lists it) - the second fetch misses; record Vary as a FACT
origin ignores the header - enumerate the unkeyed-input list with a header-name fuzzer posture (one at a time, ledgered)
poison stored but TTL shorter than your re-fetch window - measure TTL first with Age headers

prerequisites: origin builds absolute URLs from the declared scheme
entries.probe: GET /?cb={{rand}} HTTP/1.1 with X-Forwarded-Scheme: http (against an https origin)
entries.oracle: stored response carries a Location/absolute-URL downgrade (https->http) - the poisoned entry redirects victims to the http variant: open-redirect-as-poison class
failure_modes: scheme hard-coded - header ignored
HSTS on the domain converts the redirect silently in the victim browser - impact chain breaks; record the HSTS fact

entries.technique: fat GET (body accepted on GET, keyed off)
prerequisites: origin/framework reads parameters from a GET request BODY
cache keys method+path but not the body
entries.probe: GET /?cb={{rand}} HTTP/1.1 with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and body secret={{marker}}
entries.oracle: the body parameter changes the stored response; a clean GET on the same URL inherits it
failure_modes: cache refuses GET-with-body (413/400) - refusal is a FACT, class closed for this hop
origin ignores GET bodies (framework default) - test per route, frameworks differ

source.title: Practical Web Cache Poisoning (fat GET class)

prerequisites: origin reflects an unknown query parameter into the page
cache keys only SOME of the query (or normalizes unknowns out)
entries.probe: GET /?cb={{rand}}&utm_source={{marker}} HTTP/1.1, then fetch GET /?cb={{rand}} alone
entries.oracle: second fetch inherits the marker: the utm-style parameter is reflected by origin but excluded from the key
failure_modes: full-URL cache keys (all params keyed) - no inheritance; class closed, record the key structure as FACT
parameter name allowlisted by origin - reflection absent; enumerate names one at a time

entries.technique: web cache deception - extension suffix (the Gil class)
prerequisites: cache rule stores paths ending in static extensions (.css/.js/.txt)
origin (framework router) IGNORES the trailing suffix - serves the authenticated page anyway
victim session authenticated (operator-owned account for the proof)
entries.oracle: the authenticated response (session data) is stored under the public-suffix key; a second, UNAUTHENTICATED fetch of the same URL returns the cached private data - operator's own session data in the proof, always
failure_modes: origin 404s unknown suffixes (strict router) - the class dies at the router; try the delimiter set (CACHE-007) before closing
origin sets Cache-Control: private/no-store and the cache HONORS it - deception refused; record which layer held
cache requires explicit static-file rules that also key on session/cookie - no cross-user inheritance
response varies per session AND cache keys the cookie - the stored entry is only your own: impact collapses to self-deception

source.title: Web Cache Deception Attack (Black Hat USA 2017)

prerequisites: strict-router target where the plain suffix fails
entries.probe: one delimiter per probe: /profile%2Ftest.css (encoded slash) | /profile//test.css (double slash) | /profile/. (dot-segment) | /profile\test.css (backslash) | /profile;.css (semicolon path param) | /profile?.css (query form) | /profile#.css (fragment cut)
entries.oracle: cache reads a static-looking path (its parser stops at its own delimiter) while the origin's router reads the clean route - same pair-of-parsers law as desync-hunter; private response stored under the confused key
failure_modes: BOTH sides decode the delimiter identically - no disagreement, no deception; each delimiter is its own FACT record (never 'the set failed')
cache normalizes the path before keying - confused key collapses to the clean key and misses
WAF rejects encoded slashes - refusal, not a negative

source.title: Cached and Confused: Web Cache Deception in the Wild; Gotta cache 'em all

prerequisites: a cache whose static-file rule matches on one URL property while the origin routes on another
entries.probe: requests that present the same resource through different URL shapes (case, trailing content-type strings, extension-in-query, extension-in-fragment) - one shape per probe, cache buster where possible
entries.oracle: a mismatched shape where the cache stores what the origin considers dynamic - deception or poisoning depending on which side wins the disagreement
failure_modes: single-CDN stacks with consistent rules - mismatch surface small; this entry is a hunting posture, not a fixed payload

entries.technique: cache-control & Vary posture oracle (the boundary map)
prerequisites: any cache engagement - run this EARLY
entries.probe: compare response headers of static asset vs dynamic route: Cache-Control directives, Vary list, Age, X-Cache class
entries.oracle: the header set maps WHICH responses the cache will store and WHICH request properties key them - the boundary map that decides whether CACHE-002..008 are even live hypotheses
failure_modes: Cloudflare/CDN-tier overriding origin directives (edge rules force caching despite private) - probe the EDGE's real behavior, do not trust the origin header alone
Vary: User-Agent segments the cache - poisoning lands per-UA; the proof fetch must replay the same UA
treat this as a FACT record set (R-NNN), not a finding - it is the map
